spec_match.rationale: Probes the exact surface the v153 entry changes: after the fetch promise resolves, abort(sentinel) must reject a pending reader.read() and a buffering text() with the sentinel itself (fetch spec abort-fetch steps); the verdict is derived from the identity of the real rejection.

interactive.rationale: Two try-it buttons run the real chunked fetch, real abort, and render a verdict, a per-event timeline, and the raw rejection detail.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises the sentinel probe with a timeline and forwarded-vs-generic verdict; the page delivers both variants.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles endpoint failure (non-OK status renders an actionable error, never fake success), the read-resolved-before-abort race as inconclusive, and an unexpected rejection shape as its own branch.

references.rationale: Links the fetch spec abort steps, crbug.com/502133195, and the sibling matrix concept; feature index carries the ChromeStatus link.

conformance.rationale: The suite's body-reader-read-rejects-with-forwarded-reason and text-rejects-with-forwarded-reason encode this exact contract and fail honestly (false) on this pre-153 Chromium — a falsifiable probe of the v153 behaviour.

runtime_evidence.rationale: CDP driver run 2026-08-16 (f1-midstream.png): verdict GENERIC with the real message 'BodyStreamBuffer was aborted', timeline showed headers resolved before chunk-1 read and abort, text() variant reported the object-reason substitution; zero console errors; the two net::ERR_ABORTED entries are the bannered intentional cancellations.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts midstream-reason-forwarded or midstream-generic-fallback explicitly per branch (never a fake pass), plus setup-failure asserts for endpoint errors.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; verdict states use left-border accents (emerald/amber/rose) on the stone background with charcoal text, all AA.

accessibility.rationale: Verdict is a role=status element updated with text; timeline is a list; detail uses output; buttons are native with disabled state during runs and visible focus.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Feature harness passed both classes; timeline entries wrap with overflow-wrap so the mono text never forces horizontal scroll at 360px.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify the forwarded branch on a Chrome 153 build
openQuestions.detail: On this Chromium 141 only the generic pre-153 branch is observable (verified honestly). When a 153+ or ForwardReasonToFetchBodyAbort-flagged binary is available to the harness, run both probes and confirm the FORWARDED verdict path renders and the telemetry assert midstream-reason-forwarded fires.

guidanceConsulted.query: async button action result status live region error state
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce async outcomes through role=status text, not colour alone; disable the trigger while running.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The verdict element is role=status, carries explicit FORWARDED/GENERIC text, and the buttons disable during the probe with a cursor hint.

guidanceConsulted.query: streamed fetch progress and abort without unhandled rejections
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Attach rejection handlers before triggering cancellation paths to avoid unhandledrejection noise.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Both probes attach catch handlers to the pending read/text promises before calling abort(); the driver runs recorded zero console errors and no unhandled rejections.

summary: The core v153 probe: real chunked fetch, sentinel abort, identity-checked verdict with a timeline. On this pre-153 Chromium it honestly reports the generic AbortError substitution ('BodyStreamBuffer was aborted') that the feature fixes, and documents the exact flag path to see the forwarded branch today.
